app: gitlab.com: in your top-level group go to Settings > SAML SSO. Self-managed: configure the SAML OmniAuth provider in the GitLab Rails config or Admin > Settings > General (check your app's current UI).
GitLab shows its assertion consumer service URL - https://{host}/users/auth/saml/callback - and an identifier/issuer, https://{host}. Copy both into the FlareID service provider.
Set the IdP SSO target URL to {idp_sso_url} and upload the certificate or paste its SHA fingerprint from {idp_cert_url}; where offered, point GitLab at {idp_metadata_url}.
Require the NameID format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent - GitLab expects a stable identifier per user.
Save and sign in once with a GitLab-linked account before enforcing SAML for the group or instance.
flareid: Add a SAML service provider (Admin > Applications > SAML service providers > New) and apply this template.
Replace {host} with gitlab.com for SaaS group SSO or your self-managed hostname.
Keep NameID format persistent. Users link their GitLab account by email on first sign-in, so the email/name/username attributes stay configured.
The groups attribute lets GitLab group-sync read memberships where that feature is enabled; remove it if unwanted.
